question.text: A new investor subscribes to Kaveri Macro Fund (Cat III) mid-quarter. The strategy is at 5% above HWM — i.e., the existing unit NAV of Rs. 1,050 already embeds INR 50 of gains (above a HWM of Rs. 1,000) for which performance fee has NOT yet been accrued. Performance fee is 20% of gains above HWM. If the new investor subscribes via the EQUALISATION CREDIT method (Series-of-units / equalisation), what is the INITIAL offset the new investor effectively receives versus existing investors?

answer.text: A performance-fee charge equal to 20% of Rs. 50 = Rs. 10 per unit, paid upfront
An equalisation credit equal to 20% of Rs. 50 = Rs. 10 per unit, ensuring the new investor is not charged performance fee on gains that accrued BEFORE subscription
A 1% entry load credited to the fund
A bonus unit equal to 5% of subscription

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the equalisation-credit method, a new investor subscribing when the unit NAV embeds gains above the HWM receives a credit so they are not charged performance fee on returns that accrued BEFORE they entered. Here, 20% x INR 50 of pre-existing above-HWM gains = INR 10 per unit credit, ensuring the new investor is only charged performance fee on incremental gains from their subscription point forward. This preserves fairness across subscription cohorts. The Trap: Option A inverts the mechanic — an equalisation DEBIT applies when NAV is BELOW HWM at subscription, not above. Options C (entry load) and D (bonus units) are unrelated cost/structural concepts. Note: The equalisation-credit mechanism, series-of-units accounting, and the Rs. 10 per-unit offset described above are not explicitly set out in the cited XIX-E (Category III AIF Managers) workbook pages, which support HWM/performance-fee disclosure concepts generally. The framing reflects general industry practice for Category III fund accounting.
